messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up 1: Acme POC is failing for long chat payloads. They get 413 / "Payload Too Large" from their on-prem gateway. Works for short chats. Need quick triage and a short note for their infra team + a cost estimate for very long contexts.
dave_se: Can you paste their error and how they're calling the API?
maria_sales: They forwarded this snippet from their client stack:
```
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 0

{ very large JSON ~1.1MB after encoding, customer claims ~180k tokens }
```
acme_infra_bot: infra: nginx logs -> "client intended to send too large body"; app-lb logs -> "413 from downstream"
tess_eng: Short diagnosis: most likely their nginx or LB is enforcing a body size cap (default nginx ~1M). Also possible issue with chunked transfer + proxies rewriting headers so upstream sees Content-Length mismatch.
dave_se: Quick repro we can send to them:
```
# check nginx setting
grep -R "client_max_body_size" /etc/nginx || echo 'no explicit limit found'
# simulate large request
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  --data-binary @big_payload.json
```
maria_sales: They tried curling through the gateway -> 413. Curl directly to our endpoint -> 200. So gateway confirmed.
tess_eng: What immediate workarounds to propose to their infra team?
dave_se: Draft note they can paste into their ops ticket:
"Your gateway (nginx or upstream LB) is returning 413 before the request reaches our API. Please check/raise client_max_body_size in nginx.conf (for example client_max_body_size 20M;), and verify any load balancer or WAF in front of nginx doesn't enforce a smaller limit. If you use chunked transfer-encoding, ensure the LB supports streaming chunked bodies and does not expect a Content-Length header. If changes are restricted, consider: 1) uploading large context to an internal blobstore and sending a small request with a reference; 2) summarizing or retrieving only relevant chunks client-side (RAG) to shrink payloads."
maria_sales: They replied: company policy forbids presigned URLs for this POC. So option 1 is off the table for now.
tess_eng: Then recommend two paths: 1) increase gateway limits for the POC (e.g., 15-20MB) or 2) implement client-side summarization / sliding-window retrieval to reduce sent tokens. Also confirm whether they're gzipping request bodies; some middleboxes drop compressed bodies.
dave_se: Cost estimate request: customer wants rough numbers for 150k-200k token contexts at ~40 requests/day. Quick calc I sketched: 200k tokens * 40/day ~ 8M tokens/day = ~240M tokens/month input. Add output tokens (assume 1.5k per response) ~ 60M output. Total ~300M tokens/month. Multiply by hosted per-token rate -> estimate. If they move to Dedicated, unit cost may decrease depending on commit and model quantization. I'll follow up with pricing.
maria_sales: Any other immediate diagnostic logs to ask them for?
tess_eng: Ask for: full nginx access/error logs around the 413, LB error codes, whether the client is using Transfer-Encoding: chunked vs Content-Length, and a redacted example payload to sanity-check tokenization if they can share. Also ask if the gateway rewrites headers or terminates TLS (some LBs terminate and re-origin which can affect chunk handling).
dave_se: I'll send the nginx note and the checklist. Maria, can you get confirmation on whether they can temporarily relax the policy for an anonymized sample payload? That would let us verify token counts and suggest better batching.
maria_sales: I'll request the anon sample and update. Thanks. :pray:
acme_infra_bot: infra: ops updated config to client_max_body_size 16M and retesting in 10m.
maria_sales: Great. If they still need >16M we can recommend Dedicated/private with configurable front-door or work with them on RAG/summarization as a longer-term fix.
tess_eng: One-liner for their security team (paste-ready): "This is an infra limit on your side. For the POC, please increase your gateway body limit or use a retrieval/summarization pattern so each API call is <~5-10k tokens; Dedicated/private deployments can set higher ingress limits if policy allows."
dave_se: I'll add a simple checklist to the ticket: nginx client_max_body_size, LB max request size, check chunked vs non-chunked, gzip enabled, include sample redacted payload if policy allows.
maria_sales: Thanks team, will update customer.
